content.value_statement: Slow applications are difficult to diagnose across browser, service, database, and infrastructure layers. This skill structures testing, measurement, bottleneck analysis, and prioritized improvements.
actual_capabilities: Defines measurable performance goals using throughput, latency percentiles, errors, concurrency, and resource utilization.
Designs baseline, load, stress, endurance, spike, and capacity test scenarios.
Drafts k6 test scripts and recommends JMeter, Locust, wrk, or other suitable tools.
Guides diagnosis across frontend, application, JVM, database, container, and infrastructure layers.
Suggests full-stack optimizations for code, queries, caching, architecture, and deployment.
Structures performance reports with environments, scenarios, trends, bottlenecks, recommendations, and release conclusions.
limitations: It does not include performance tools, monitoring services, or a runnable test harness.
It cannot guarantee results without representative traffic, production-scale data, and complete telemetry.
Its example thresholds and commands require adaptation to each system and operating environment.
Load tests and diagnostics require authorization, controlled targets, and human review before execution.

use_cases.title: Plan a Release Load Test
use_cases.description: Define targets, traffic stages, observability needs, acceptance criteria, and a controlled execution plan before a major release.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Slow Application
use_cases.description: Connect latency symptoms with frontend traces, service metrics, database plans, resource saturation, and prioritized experiments.

use_cases.title: Estimate Service Capacity
use_cases.description: Use measured throughput and resource trends to identify limits, scaling needs, and operational headroom.

prompt_templates.title: Define Performance Goals
prompt_templates.prompt: Help define performance goals for [system]. Users perform [workflows], expected traffic is [traffic], and the current environment is [environment].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a performance review with measurable targets.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Load Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a load test plan for [endpoint or workflow]. Include traffic stages, test data, checks, thresholds, monitoring, risks, and stop conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a controlled test before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Bottleneck
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these measurements from [system]: [metrics]. Correlate latency, errors, throughput, resources, traces, and queries. Rank likely causes and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn observed telemetry into testable hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Capacity and Optimization Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [test results] and [architecture], estimate capacity, identify constraints, compare optimization options, and propose phased changes with validation criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce an advanced cross-layer improvement roadmap.

output_examples.input: Design a load test for a checkout API expecting 300 requests per second.
output: Baseline: verify one-user behavior and response correctness.
Ramp: increase traffic to 300 requests per second while monitoring latency and errors.
Hold: sustain expected traffic, then test controlled headroom.
Stop when error rate, latency, or resource safeguards exceed approved limits.

output_examples.input: Our API latency rises while CPU stays low and database connections reach their limit.
output_examples.output: The leading hypothesis is connection pool saturation or leakage. Compare active, idle, waiting, and timeout trends before changing pool size.

output_examples.input: Create a concise performance report outline.
output: Scope, environment, workload, and acceptance criteria
Throughput, latency percentiles, errors, and resource trends
Release conclusion, risks, and validation actions

best_practices: Run tests against authorized, isolated environments with agreed safeguards and stop conditions.
Collect application, database, infrastructure, and client metrics before increasing load.
Change one variable at a time and repeat tests to confirm each optimization.
anti_patterns: Do not run unapproved load tests against production or third-party services.
Do not optimize from average latency alone; inspect percentiles, errors, throughput, and saturation together.
Do not claim capacity from a single short test or an unrepresentative data set.

faq.question: Does this skill execute performance tests?
faq.answer: It provides plans, examples, diagnostic guidance, and report structures. Execution depends on available tools, permissions, and the selected environment.

faq.question: Which load testing tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It discusses k6, JMeter, Locust, Gatling, wrk, Vegeta, and Apache Bench for different workloads.

faq.question: Can it help with frontend performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Lighthouse, browser diagnostics, code splitting, lazy loading, image optimization, caching, and content delivery.

faq.question: Can it diagnose database bottlenecks?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides query plan review, slow query analysis, lock investigation, indexing, connection pools, and database monitoring.

faq.question: Does it support capacity planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It relates load levels, throughput, latency, errors, and resource saturation to estimate limits and scaling needs.

faq.question: Is production load testing safe?
faq.answer: Production testing needs explicit authorization, safeguards, observability, stop conditions, and a recovery plan. An isolated environment is preferred.
